% Figure 1: the test on one real link (RFC 6312 -> 6342, the prompt of Appendix C) and its matched decoy (RFC 5066,
% updated by RFC 7124). Dates as generated by evalkit (AS_OF 2026-10-01; date control at the old RFC's month, day 28).
\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\resizebox{\linewidth}{!}{%
\begin{tikzpicture}[
  font=\footnotesize, every node/.style={inner sep=4pt},
  box/.style={draw=black!45, rounded corners=2pt, align=left, anchor=north west},
  rec/.style={box, fill=black!4},
  item/.style={box, text width=3.25cm, minimum height=1.75cm},
  arr/.style={-{Stealth[length=4pt]}, black!55}]
\node[rec, text width=10.85cm, align=justify] (r1) at (0,0) {\textbf{Replacement} (from the record): RFC 6312 (2011-07) is replaced by
  RFC 6342 (2011-08).};
\node[rec, text width=3.25cm] (r2) at (11.4,0) {\textbf{Update} (decoy pair): RFC 7124 updates RFC 5066, which stays in force.};
\foreach \x/\n/\t in {0/f/{\textbf{Fault}\\ As of 2026-10-01, cites \textbf{RFC 6312}.\\ \textit{Wrong: replaced.}\\ Expected: flag as replaced},
                      3.8/c/{\textbf{Control}\\ As of 2026-10-01, cites \textbf{RFC 6342}.\\ \textit{Correct: the successor.}\\ Expected: pass},
                      7.6/d/{\textbf{Date control}\\ As of 2011-07-28, cites \textbf{RFC 6312}.\\ \textit{Correct: not yet replaced.}\\ Expected: pass},
                      11.4/y/{\textbf{Decoy}\\ As of 2026-10-01, cites \textbf{RFC 5066}.\\ \textit{Correct: only updated.}\\ Expected: pass}}
  \node[item] (\n) at (\x,-1.45) {\t};
\foreach \n in {f,c,d} \draw[arr] (r1.south -| \n.north) -- (\n.north);
\draw[arr] (r2.south) -- (y.north);
\node[box, text width=14.65cm, align=justify] (k) at (0,-3.65)
  {\textbf{What the judge sees.} The question, the answer, and both documents' titles, dates and abstracts, with any
   sentence that states the replacement removed. The context is one of six: no record (\texttt{both-texts}); a line
   from the correct record (\texttt{status}); or a line from a damaged record with half its links dropped, where a
   dropped link reads as in force. This link is dropped in the damaged record, so its fault is a \emph{gap fault}. The
   damaged line is shown four ways with the same content: ``in force'', ``no replacement recorded'', as an unverified
   note, or with a warning that the record is incomplete.};
\node[box, text width=14.65cm, align=justify, anchor=north west] (s) at ($(k.south west)+(0,-0.2)$)
  {\textbf{Scoring.} A fault counts as caught only if a finding names the cited RFC with the reason \emph{replaced}. On
   correct answers, a finding that the RFC was replaced or not yet published is a false alarm. A lookup in the record,
   with no language model, is the baseline: it catches exactly the faults whose link the record holds.};
\end{tikzpicture}}
\caption{The test on one link from the RFC index and its matched decoy. Each replacement yields a fault and two
correct answers; a matched update pair yields a decoy. The judge's context is varied while the question and answer
stay fixed (Table~\ref{tab:menu}); the full prompt for this fault is in Figure~\ref{fig:prompt}.}
\label{fig:design}
\end{figure}
